item.title: Ethan Mollick：An illustration of both the power and issues with Astra 6.2 in a way that mi…
item.description:
An illustration of both the power and issues with Astra 6.2 in a way that might be accessible: I asked it to create a game in Blender and Unity where you are the pilot of a Coast Guard cutter who travelled back in time to the War of Independence to stop the British invasion of New York.

It made incredible 3D models and a working game with no errors - its even fun to play! But Astra got obsessed with random ideas that didn't make a lot of sense and built them out without asking along with following my instructions: you could put down false buoys to lure the ship in the wrong direction (like the British would understand a modern buoy?) or you could persuade the British ships to go the wrong direction by talking to them, or that you would spend your time rescuing sailors from other parts of the harbor. It didn't even initially have a shooting mechanism until I pointed it out. This is all kind of minor stuff individually, but it was frustrating to have the AI constantly do its own things without telling me, given its instincts were often off, and then have to redirect it constantly. Other models, including GPT-6 Asta, didn't require the same struggle to control and operate. And these same issues show up in academic research and other more serious use cases.

item.title: Ethan Mollick：A favorite optimistic view of the future of AI is from a pessimistic book th…
item.description:
A favorite optimistic view of the future of AI is from a pessimistic book that not about AI: "Rise and Fall of American Growth," which argues that we had a one-time explosion in living standards from 1870 and 1920 (& later outside the US).

In 1870: no toilets, no city plumbing, lamp light, no central heating, little public health, horses for local travel, etc. In 50 years, all of this was solved & the nation was electrified. In the next fifty modern medicine, air travel and telecommunication happened.

The book then points out that we have had no changes in lifestyle of similar scale since the 1970s. Written in 2016, it argued that we would likely never experience another boom like the "Special Century." The positive view of AI should make us ask "But what if we do?" and "How do we make it all go right?"

item.title: Ethan Mollick：I spent a decent amount of time with Gemini 4 before launch. Overall, Gemini…
item.description:
I spent a decent amount of time with Gemini 4 before launch. Overall, Gemini 4 is a big jump over previous Gemini models and it is the first non-OpenAI/Anthropic model to pass the Fable/Mythos/Astra bar. It is also much more pleasant and more agentic then previous Gemini models, without the weird personality issues that you often found in Gemini 3 series models. In fact, a big advantage is that has a very different personality and sense of taste than Claude or Astra, making it a good addition to the AI world.

On the usefulness side, in some areas it is at least at par with OpenAI and Anthropic (it is quite creative and a good writer), but in others it lags, including at complex multi-agent work. It has a tendency to be too certain about its conclusions and a little lazy, issues not helped by the Antigravity harness not being quite as good as the competition. Still, I expect to see rapid improvements in model abilities using Gemini 4 as a base.

Here is a fun example: "create the ultimate brutalist city builder. you should have lots of controls over buildings in ways that are delightful and inuitive to people who just want to play, but are sophisticated and deep for people who know something about architecture. you should be able to play a lot with design and approach. there should be simulation modes and different ways to view or experience the city. make it stunning. i want to host this on netlify in the end"

Astra Max in Codex: https://t.co/lyalJY4E4g
5.1 Max in Code: https://t.co/WNt4lA05B6
Argon in Antigravity: https://t.co/7gUAuCA49J
